'''James L. Kinsey''' (October 15, 1934, in [[Paris, Texas]] &ndash; December 20, 2014, in [[Houston|Houston, Texas]])<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chemistry.mit.edu/james-l-kinsey-1934-2014 |title=James L. Kinsey, 1934-2014 &#124; MIT Department of Chemistry |access-date=2015-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150124000713/http://chemistry.mit.edu/james-l-kinsey-1934-2014 |archive-date=2015-01-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  was an American [[chemist]], and D. R. Bullard-Welch Foundation Professor at [[Rice University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chemistry.rice.edu/FacultyDetail.aspx?RiceID=592 |title=James Kinsey : Rice University Department of Chemistry |access-date=2011-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120602210818/http://chemistry.rice.edu/FacultyDetail.aspx?RiceID=592 |archive-date=2012-06-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
He won the 1995 Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=James&last_nm=Kinsey&year=1995|title = Prize Recipient}}</ref>
He was a 1969 [[Guggenheim Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/7874-james-l-kinsey |title=James L. Kinsey - John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |accessdate=2011-10-30 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130104134505/http://www.gf.org/fellows/7874-james-l-kinsey |archivedate=2013-01-04 }}</ref> He was a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

==Life==
He graduated from Rice University, with a B.A. in 1956 and PhD in 1959.
He studied the [[University of Upsala]], and the [[University of California, Berkeley]].
He taught at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1962 to 1988.
